title: Repeated rows reduced standard errors by 29-30 percent under independent errors in four coral heat models, 2003-2019
abstract: We tested whether repeated substrate rows change heat slopes and calculated precision in BCO-DMO coral data. Four Atlantic and Pacific models for 2003-2019 used 9,623 Reef Check sample IDs and 19,196 flat rows. Models controlled country, year, calendar month and depth. Counting flat rows reduced standard errors by 29.0-30.0 percent under independent errors. Slopes changed by less than 0.09 bleaching percentage points per four TSA degree-heating weeks. Site- and country-grouped standard errors changed by less than 1.5 percent. Separate expanded-row regressions and an exact uniform-repeat identity checked the calculations. The result is a fixed-file precision audit, not a causal heat estimate or a claim of error in prior studies. Missing outcomes, selected visits, site confounding and dependence across groups remain. The package gives sample evidence, row counts, code, source hashes, checks and a figure.

display.caption: Heat slopes change little when repeated substrate rows count as separate surveys. Independent-error standard errors fall by about 30 percent; grouped standard errors stay close. The country intervals are approximate four-test working intervals.
